newsitem.title: USA: ComEd sees Quad Cities nuke back next week.
newsitem.headline: ComEd sees Quad Cities nuke back next week.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co said Tuesday it expects its 789 megawatt (MW) Quad Cities nuclear power unit 1 to return to service early next week following a shutdown for repairs.
"(The shutdown) is going to take a few days," said company spokesman Gary Wald, adding "it looks like early next week (for a restart)."
Quad Cities 1, located in Cordova, Ill., will shut later today to repair an electronic relay system, Wald said.
As of early Tuesday, the unit was operating at 60 percent of capacity and was reducing power in anticipation of the shutdown.
The Quad Cities 1 shutdown will bring to six the number of ComEd nuclear power units which are out of service, either for repairs or scheduled refueling and maintenance.
The total capacity out of service, including Quad Cities unit 1, is 5,814 MW.
Despite the outages, Wald said ComEd was having no difficulty meeting its supply commitments, and continued to purchase spot power on the open market as a matter of routine.
"We are always (purchasing on the spot market), often the economics make it less expensive to buy outside power," Wald said.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
